findings.claim: Mark scheme for the appearance-vs-reality essay tells students to use “Precise quotations (“all that glisters is not gold,” “look like the innocent flower”)”.
findings.truth: “Look like th’ innocent flower, / But be the serpent under’t” is Lady Macbeth, Macbeth 1.5. It is not in The Merchant of Venice. A student quoting it in a Merchant answer loses AO1 and AO2 credit. Replaced with Bassanio’s casket line, “the world is still deceiv’d with ornament” (3.2).
findings.evidence: grep of scripts/_retrofc/_texts/merchant-of-venice.txt: no match for “innocent flower” or “serpent under”; “The world is still deceiv’d with ornament.” at line 2196 (3.2).

findings.claim: Exam-technique model sentence: “A Jacobean audience, for whom mercy was a Christian duty, would have found Shylock’s refusal shocking”.
findings.truth: The play was written c.1596–97, in the reign of Elizabeth I. The Jacobean period begins in 1603. Lesson 1 and the rest of this unit correctly say “Elizabethan”. As a modelled AO3 sentence this teaches a wrong contextual label.
findings.evidence: L1 content_html: “written around 1596–1597, during the reign of Queen Elizabeth I”; spec 3.1.1 sets the Shakespeare text list only, so the date claim rests on the lesson’s own (correct) L1 statement.

findings.claim: Knowledge check 4 stem: “The three AQA assessment objectives for Shakespeare are AO1 (quotation), AO2 (language and _____), and AO3 (context).”
findings.truth: AQA 8702 Paper 1 Section A is marked on four AOs: AO1, AO2, AO3 and AO4 (accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar), which carries the extra 4 marks in the 30+4 total. The same lesson’s content_html says “four assessment objectives” and its exam tip says “30+4”, so the knowledge check contradicts its own lesson. The keyed answer (“structure”) stays correct; only the stem is wrong.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2: AO1–AO4 listed; 4.2 weighting table gives AO4 to both papers. L7 content_html n25: “judged across four assessment objectives”.

findings.claim: Shylock quoted as “Let no sound of shallow foppery enter / My sober house” (Act 2, Scene 5).
findings.truth: The line is “Let not the sound of shallow fopp’ry enter / My sober house.” The act and scene are right; the wording is not. Corrected to “Let not the sound of shallow foppery enter”.

findings.claim: Practice question 4 says “Refer to Act 3, Scene 1 in your answer”, and its top band requires “the ‘my daughter! my ducats!’ report through Solanio”.
findings.truth: Solanio’s “My daughter! O my ducats! O my daughter!” report is Act 2, Scene 8. The rubric therefore asks for material outside the scene it names. Question widened to “Act 2, Scene 8 and Act 3, Scene 1” and the mark scheme now names the real scene.

findings.claim: Under the Act 3 heading: “Solanio reports that Shylock ran through the streets crying ‘My daughter! O my ducats! O my daughter!’”, with no act or scene given.
findings.truth: The report is Act 2, Scene 8. In an Act 3 lesson with no reference attached, students will cite it as 3.1 in a closed-book exam. Scene reference added; nothing else changed.

findings.claim: Flashcard answer: “A monkey — a callous trade for Shylock’s wedding gift.”
findings.truth: Shylock says “It was my turquoise, I had it of Leah when I was a bachelor” — Leah gave him the ring before the marriage, so it is not a wedding gift. The same lesson quotes that line, so the flashcard contradicts its own source.

findings.claim: Every lesson labels its short questions “8 marks — Extract Analysis” or “4 marks — Quote Analysis” (28 questions across the unit).
findings.truth: Neither label matches an AQA 8702 question. Paper 1 Section A is one 30+4 extract-plus-whole-text question and nothing else. Several so-labelled questions also contradict their own label — L1 Q4/Q5 and L7 Q4/Q5 are “Extract Analysis” with no extract; L1 Q6 and L7 Q6 are “Quote Analysis” with no quotation. The “30+4 marks — Shakespeare Essay” labels are correct. This is house format across the EngLit units, so it belongs in the programme-wide relabel queue rather than a per-unit edit.
findings.evidence: spec section 2, Paper 1: “Section A Shakespeare: students will answer one question on their play of choice”, 64 marks total across both sections.

findings.claim: L3 names the taunters in 3.1 as “Solanio and Salerio”; L2 names Antonio’s friends as “Salarino and Solanio”. L1 and L6 quote the extract cue as “Signor Antonio, many a time and oft”.
findings.truth: The base text has Solanio and Salarino in 3.1, and “Signior Antonio” at 1.3. Editions differ — several modern texts merge Salarino into Salerio — so neither naming is wrong in itself, but the unit is inconsistent with itself. Not worth an edit that would ripple through narration.
findings.evidence: merchant-of-venice.txt line 1909 (3.1 “Enter Solanio and Salarino”), line 706 (“Signior Antonio, many a time and oft”).

summary: Seven lessons checked against the Gutenberg text and the AQA 8702 spec; every other quotation, speaker and act/scene attribution verified correct, and all 35 knowledge-check keys are right. One HIGH: a Macbeth line (“look like the innocent flower”) is prescribed as a Merchant quotation in an L7 mark scheme. Five MEDIUM fixes follow: a Jacobean/Elizabethan context error, a knowledge check that denies AO4 on the Shakespeare question, a misquoted 2.5 line, and a 2.8/3.1 scene misattribution in L3.
